title: Made a Voice AI game demo—interested in feedback!
author: maxchild
selftext:
Hi all, first time poster, long-time lurker. 

Launching a Voice AI game today called “Wit’s End”. It’s in the style of Dungeons and Dragons, but sillier/more deranged. Would love feedback or if anyone wants to do an official playtest lmk! Can play here at [https://witsend.ai](https://witsend.ai) 

Best enjoyed with friends on your desktop web browser. Mobile coming soon + additional levels past level 1!

comments.author: Manticore-9292
comments.body: Your ads on other sub-reddits forgot to mention it's voice and not text.

replies.author: maxchild
replies.body: Good feedback—will fix! You can use "text only" mode if you like but that's definitely not the core way to play.

replies.author: Manticore-9292
replies.body: Thanks. Meow does not \*\*have\*\* a microphone nor camera. Meow is a familiar, not the sorcerer who summoned meow.

replies.author: Manticore-9292
replies.body: Got a ways into a game. Nice work. Errors kicked meow from the room though. Will try to return later since the miscommunication message did not give any info as to why this happened.

replies.author: maxchild
replies.body: We are investigating—obviously way too many issues! Apologies and will post here once we've figured out the source and fixed the problem. Thanks so much again for letting us know.

replies.author: Manticore-9292
replies.body: It seems to be working without the problem now. I managed to complete a basic run-through. Should be interesting when further story arcs are added.

replies.author: maxchild
replies.body: Appreciate the feedback—we aren't handling sessions with long pauses right now well so working on a fix to that issue. Stay tuned, should have a fix soon!

comments.author: TheRealErikMalkavian
comments.body: I'll give it a shot and let you know what I experienced.  Thanks!

comments.author: Noobsauce9001
comments.body:
Hey, I just tried your game, pretty impressed! I used your feedback feature to leave a couple responses.   
  
The two parts that impressed me the most were the character consistency in the art generation, as well as how quickly the voice based AI responses were generated. Well done!

replies.author: maxchild
replies.body: Thanks so much! We read all the feedback so I appreciate it. Let me know which parts you'd like to improve.

comments.author: 9spaceking
comments.body: Not bad, you should inform users of the limitations and the ideas going on here. I tried surrendering to guards and go to prison but I got sent to tavern instead. I destroyed the tavern but got sent to the forest. A good start but definitely could use some polishing

replies.author: maxchild
replies.body: We are working on unchaining these limitations very soon...stay tuned!

replies.author: Inevitable-Dig8702
replies.body:
I kept trying to convince the guard that my business in town involved his mum and while I appreciated the chuckles from the other guards, I didn't quite get the visceral response I was goading him for.  A tall order for your game to support derailment like this, but then classic CRPG games would often have the entire town coming after me (Think Ultima I!) if I tried to smack an NPC.

But then I thought to myself : This is exactly where I was on Year 1, Month 1, Week 1 as a newbie TTRPG DM.  I would constantly plot-hammer my fledgling PCs away from any "funny business" but I eventually evolved and would gladly  now spend an entire night's session on a ad-hoc episode entitled "The Business with the Guard Captain's Mum".

Very promising stuff and I hope to see your system evolve as well!

comments.author: octalgorilla8
comments.body:
I started trying Wits End today and have determined that I'm going to channel all the energy from My Little Pony to play a mint green pony named Jolly with a Book of Time. Admittedly, I'm kind of surprised that the AI DM allowed me to get such a perceptually powerful weapon. I'm taking a completely pacifist approach to the game. Dmitri enjoyed having a vision of my happy homeland and was thoroughly charmed by my kindness. It took a while to get through the tavern because I didn't have any real in-character motivation to get the letter.

Do you know if a complete pacifist run is possible?

Also, I noticed I accidentally quit the game instead of logging out. This kicked me back to the start. You may want to look at revising to "Save and Quit" or something similar to clarify how to save progress vs. restarting.

replies.author: maxchild
replies.body:
Hahaha I haven't tried a pacifist run but interested in your feedback on how it goes. Charm is definitely a load-bearing option!

Yes I agree with you on the saving/progress, we are working on this.

comments.author: VirinaB
comments.body:
Hey there, just tried the game after seeing the ads on Reddit (one of the rare ads that was upvoted, so congrats). When we play AI games you always give things some slack, and accept that it's all very *approximate*. With that in mind, I really liked the what I saw with regard to the cinematics and character creation and the GPT-like illustrations.

I left my feedback on the overall story because I found it confusing. To be clear, I'm not referring to the stuff in-game. I know that LLMs can get confused and some things can feel very "dream-like" in that details don't remain consistent. What I'm referring to though is the story in the cinematics.

The closing cinematics for the first adventure dumped a lot of information at once. Is there some place where it's written down so I can better make sense of what's going on? If not, can you create one for "The Story So Far"

replies.author: maxchild
replies.body: Agree with the feedback, and thanks! We are working on updating the cinematics to make them more clear/coherent, so stay tuned—we definitely agree with your take. We are also working on consistency with the LLM-driven details, should see some progress there soon.

comments.author: 2snakey4u
comments.body:
I just started this game and  so much fun playing as a sneaky elven archer! The character creation was spot-on for my written description, and it was impressive how consistent my character looked in each plot-related illustration. My character's story felt cohesive, too, like a comic book based on a 90s Saturday morning cartoon. It felt immersive, not weird or slop-ish. I especially enjoyed the dialogue options, and ability to joke around and banter with the characters (especially the castle guards!)

Since I couldn't find any other place to gush, I came here (hope I'm not too late to join this thread.) I play boardgames IRL and online, and it's nice to be able to play D&D on my phone as a "solo player" when my IRL friends aren't available.

The only thing I could not figure out was how to save my progress on my phone (and not just save my character.) Sadly, I lost all my progress twice and got send back to the start (I did not quit the game or turn off my phone, I just switched windows and came back to find myself back at the start.) Despite that, I had so much fun, and plan to try again!

So, overall, I think you've build a fantastic game, and the only feature I'd love is to see is an easy way to save my story progress on mobile (so that I can level my character up over time and explore more of the environment)

replies.author: maxchild
replies.body: Thanks so much! Please leave any other feedback—we aim to keep improving the game over the next several months.
